biography: James Courtney, the 'Outback Ace,' was born in the dusty mining town of Broken Hill, Australia. His racing journey began not on tarmac, but on the treacherous dirt tracks of outback motocross, where he honed his reflexes and fearless approach. A chance encounter with a touring V8 Supercar team ignited a passion for four wheels, leading him to scrape together enough funds to enter the state-level Formula Ford series. He quickly rose through the ranks, showcasing a raw talent and tenacity that belied his age. Courtney's peak came in the late 20s, securing multiple podiums in premier series and earning the respect of veterans. Now in his mid-30s, driving for Mobius Autosports, he's struggling to recapture that glory, facing a new generation of drivers who seem to have unlocked a different level of performance. Yet, the fire still burns, fueled by a deep-seated belief in his own abilities, even as whispers of retirement grow louder.
drivingStyle: Courtney's driving style is a study in controlled aggression, a legacy of his motocross background. He's known for late-braking maneuvers and an uncanny ability to place his car precisely where he wants it on the track. While capable of blistering pace, his tire management can be inconsistent, often pushing too hard early in a stint and suffering later. Under pressure, Courtney tends to become more defensive, prioritizing track position over outright speed, a strategy that sometimes yields points but rarely wins races.

rivalries.reason: A clash of egos and contrasting driving styles. Rossi, known for her smooth and calculated approach, often publicly criticized Courtney's aggressive tactics, fueling a heated on-track rivalry.

Nakamura, a rising star from Japan, consistently out-qualified and out-raced Courtney in their shared season, leading to resentment and accusations of preferential treatment within the Mobius Autosports team.

Vance, a flamboyant showman, and Courtney were frequently battling for the same track position, their aggressive duels often ending in contact and heated exchanges in the paddock. Their contrasting personalities only served to amplify the rivalry.

quirks: Always wears a specific lucky pair of socks, gifted to him by his grandmother, for every race.
Listens to the same AC/DC album before every qualifying session.
Has a detailed notebook where he meticulously records every lap and setting adjustment, treating it like a sacred text.
famousQuote: "They can have the trophies and the headlines. I'm here to race, to push myself and my machine to the absolute limit. Everything else is just noise."
careerHighlight: Winning the Bathurst 1000 in 2018, a hard-fought victory achieved after battling mechanical issues and relentless pressure from rivals in the closing laps. He held off a charging Rossi by mere tenths of a second, cementing his place in Australian motorsport history.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final race of the 2020 championship due to a mechanical failure, costing him a potential title victory. The disappointment was compounded by the fact that it was his teammate who ultimately clinched the championship.
